definition: Frequency of cardiac ventricular contractions measured per minute via Lead-II electrocardiogram vector or optical photoplethysmography.
citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 §4.1; Hughson et al., 'Cardiovascular regulation in microgravity,' J Appl Physiol, 2018.
appImplementation: Continuous 1 Hz streaming on Dashboard, animated cardiac ticker, interactive telemetry table.
limitations: Prototype displays simulated 1 Hz telemetry; does not substitute for real-time 12-lead diagnostic telemetry.

definition: Root mean square of successive differences between normal heartbeat intervals, reflecting autonomic parasympathetic tone.
sourceOrg: NASA Life Sciences Data Archive / Russian IBMP
citation: Baevsky et al., 'Autonomic cardiovascular regulation in spaceflight,' Acta Astronautica, 2011; LSDA-0042.
appImplementation: Computed R-R interval analysis, autonomic balance indicator in Cardiovascular panel.
limitations: Estimated from simulated interbeat intervals; cannot establish clinical arrhythmia diagnosis.

definition: Percentage of arterial hemoglobin oxygenation measured non-invasively via dual-wavelength optical pulse oximetry.
citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 §6.3; FAA Office of Commercial Space Transportation Physiological Guidelines.
appImplementation: Primary vital card #02, Rule CDSS-O2-01 trigger, EVA Hypoxia scenario playback.
limitations: Simulated pulse oximetry stream; in real flight, cold peripheral vasoconstriction or motion artifact can cause false drops.

definition: Number of respiratory cycles per minute, monitored via chest bio-impedance or photoplethysmographic respiration modulation.
citation: CSA Bio-Monitor Astroskin Flight Validation, Expedition 58/59; NPJ Microgravity, 2021.
appImplementation: Vital card #03, respiratory waveform interpolation, concordance cross-check with SpO₂.
limitations: Synthetically interpolated from 1 Hz CSV data; physical speech or swallowing artifacts are not simulated.

concept: Systemic Blood Pressure & Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP)
definition: Hydrostatic pressure exerted by blood on arterial vessel walls. MAP = DBP + 1/3(SBP - DBP).
citation: Norsk et al., 'Fluid shifts and cardiovascular regulation in spaceflight,' Physiol Rep, 2015.
appImplementation: Calculated indicator in Cardiovascular modal, correlated with cephalad fluid shift.
limitations: Indirectly estimated from baseline parameters; true continuous arterial pressure requires continuous finger-cuff photoplethysmography.

definition: Internal hypothalamic thermal equilibrium. Microgravity impairs convective and evaporative heat dissipation, raising baseline core temperature by ~1.0°C.
citation: Stahn et al., 'Increased core body temperature in astronauts during long-duration space missions,' Sci Rep, 2017.
appImplementation: Vital card #04, thermal trend tracking, environmental heat-load alert.
limitations: Simulated telemetry; operational spaceflight measurement requires double-sensor heat-flux forehead probes.

definition: Atmospheric CO₂ partial pressure and concentration inside spacecraft pressurized volume. At 760 mmHg, 0.31% vol corresponds to 2.36 mmHg.
citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 §6.2.2; Law et al., 'Relationship Between CO2 Levels and Headaches on ISS,' J Occup Environ Med, 2014.
appImplementation: Vital card #04 badge, Rule CDSS-ENV-01, Environmental telemetry monitor.
limitations: Assumes standard total pressure of 760 mmHg (101.3 kPa). Deep-space vessels operating at 8.2 psi (56.5 kPa) require re-calculated partial pressures.

definition: Absorbed and equivalent dosimetric flux from Galactic Cosmic Rays and Solar Particle Events.
nominalRange: ISS LEO: 0.35 – 0.50 mSv/day; Deep Space Transit: 1.50 – 2.00 mSv/day; SPE Alert: > 5.00 mSv/day
citation: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 §4.4; Cucinotta et al., 'Space radiation cancer risk projections,' NASA/TP-2013-217375.
appImplementation: Environmental badge, Scenario 4 (Solar Storm Flare) playback, storm shelter alert.
limitations: Illustrative sensor values; actual mission biodosimetry requires active silicon detectors and physical tissue equivalent proportional counters.

definition: Retrobulbar optic nerve sheath diameter measured 3 mm behind the globe via high-frequency B-mode ocular ultrasound.
citation: Lee et al., 'Spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome,' NPJ Microgravity, 2020; NASA HRP SANS Evidence Report.
appImplementation: Body Map ocular node, Scenario 5 playback, Rule CDSS-SANS-01.
limitations: Illustrative ultrasound research threshold. In terrestrial medicine ONSD > 5.8 mm indicates elevated ICP; in spaceflight SANS, retrobulbar sheath distension reflects cephalad venous stasis and localized orbital CSF compartmentation without systemic malignant intracranial hypertension.

definition: Fluid pressure within the anterior chamber of the eye measured via rebound or applanation tonometry.
citation: Mader et al., 'Optic disc edema, globe flattening, and hyperopic shifts in astronauts,' Ophthalmology, 2011.
appImplementation: Ocular biometric panel, correlated with cephalad fluid shift.
limitations: Single-point values; does not capture circadian IOP fluctuation or trabecular outflow resistance.

definition: Near-infrared low-coherence interferometric cross-sectional scanning measuring peripapillary Retinal Nerve Fiber Layer (RNFL) thickness.
nominalRange: Total average RNFL thickness: 85 – 110 µm; Papilledema alert: > 125 µm
sourceOrg: NASA HRP / Columbus Module ISS Facility
citation: Patel et al., 'OCT imaging of optic disc edema in astronauts,' JAMA Ophthalmol, 2018.
appImplementation: Body Map ophthalmic diagnostic card, SANS progression tracker.
limitations: Digital visualization of clinical findings; software does not process raw OCT B-scan raw raster interferometry files.

definition: Synchronization of endogenous 24-hr suprachiasmatic circadian rhythm using Solid-State Light Assemblies (SSLA) to counter 16 sunrises/day.
nominalRange: Wake: 6500K blue-enriched (> 400 lx); Pre-sleep: 2700K warm amber (< 100 lx)
sourceOrg: NASA Human Factors / Thomas Jefferson University
citation: Brainard et al., 'Solid-state light assemblies on the ISS for circadian entrainment,' Curr Biol, 2016.
appImplementation: Rule CDSS-ENV-04, environmental lighting schedule, Circadian sleep staging.
limitations: Illustrative schedule; does not measure biological melatonin or dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO).

definition: Preservation of bone mineral density in weight-bearing skeleton (lumbar spine, femoral neck) countering microgravity osteopenia.
nominalRange: Target: > 95.0% baseline retention; Unmitigated spaceflight loss rate: ~1.0-1.5% per month
citation: Sibonga et al., 'Recovery of bone density after long-duration spaceflight,' J Bone Miner Res, 2017.
appImplementation: Mission Readiness Pillar #6 (weight 10%, score 98%), ARED workout telemetry.
limitations: Mathematical model of bone loading; actual BMD assessment requires dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) pre/post flight.

definition: Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT) assessing sustained behavioral alertness, sleep debt, and psychomotor speed.
nominalRange: Mean reaction time: < 250 ms (Optimal); Lapses (> 500 ms): <= 2 per 3-min session
sourceOrg: University of Pennsylvania / NASA Behavioral Health
citation: Basner et al., 'Psychomotor vigilance testing on the International Space Station,' Aerosp Med Hum Perform, 2015.
appImplementation: Mission Readiness Pillar #4 (weight 15%, score 95%), Neuro-cognitive status card.
limitations: Static test indicator; does not administer an active millisecond-accurate user reaction test in browser.

definition: Daily 2.0–2.5 hour operational exercise countermeasure combining resistive loading (ARED) and cycle ergometry (CEVIS).
nominalRange: ARED: up to 600 lbs simulated load; CEVIS: 150 – 220 Watts at 75–85% VO2 peak
citation: English et al., 'High-intensity resistive and aerobic exercise preserves muscle mass in spaceflight,' NPJ Microgravity, 2020.
appImplementation: Mission Readiness Pillar #1 (weight 25%, score 96%), Scenario 3 playback.
limitations: Simulated workout data; does not log physical load cell telemetry from actual gym hardware.

definition: Operational countermeasure applying negative pressure (-20 to -35 mmHg) to lower extremities to pull cephalad venous fluid caudal.
nominalRange: Protocol: -20 to -35 mmHg for 30–60 minutes daily
citation: Hargens et al., 'Lower body negative pressure as a countermeasure for spaceflight deconditioning,' Front Physiol, 2021.
appImplementation: Scenario 5 recovery step, SANS fluid shift protocol, Quest interaction.
limitations: Simulated countermeasure efficacy; individual cardiovascular tolerance and presyncopal risk vary.
